key_insight: A recurrent automatic speech recognition (ASR) system spontaneously organizes its layers to mirror human auditory cortex: different model layers map to distinct cortical regions and together encode a parallel hierarchy from acoustic → phonetic → lexical → semantic representations.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between computational speech models and brain function by showing how internal representations of a recurrent ASR align with spatially distributed linguistic processing in the human auditory cortex, clarifying whether and how models recapitulate hierarchical linguistic encoding observed in the brain.
method: Record neural responses from human auditory cortex during natural speech listening and extract activations from a trained recurrent ASR on the same stimuli.

Use encoding models and representational similarity analyses to map model layers onto cortical sites and to track which linguistic levels (acoustic, phonetic, lexical, semantic) each layer/region encodes.
Quantify a parallel progression across model depth and cortical anatomy showing coexisting, layered representations rather than a single serial transformation.
impact: Demonstrates that practical ASR systems learn brain-like, spatially distributed linguistic representations, informing model interpretability, evaluation against neural data, and the design of neuro-inspired speech architectures or diagnostics.
visual_elements: Brain map overlay: cortical surface colored by which model layer best predicts each region (layer→region mapping).
Stacked model diagram: RNN layers with arrows showing progression from waveform → acoustic features → phonetic units → lexical → semantic.
Representational similarity heatmap: model layers (rows) vs. cortical sites (columns) showing correlation strengths.
Timeline/flow graphic: example speech waveform annotated with where acoustic, phonetic, lexical and semantic representations emerge in time and across layers.
paper_title: Parallel hierarchical encoding of linguistic representations in the human auditory cortex and recurrent automatic speech recognition systems
paper_authors: Menoua Keshishian, Gavin Mischler, Samuel Thomas, Brian Kingsbury, Stephan Bickel
